libpcap is part of 2 of my public repositories, from 2014 to 2016.

What it was for: [Security and OSINT](@/projects/security.md) (1) and [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (1).

Most recently: [charon](@/work/charon.md): Ferryman who carries other people connections to other side. Operation Area? Wi-Fi!; [peacemaker](@/work/peacemaker.md): Packet sniffing and processing engine.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses libpcap: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links libpcap to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
